findings.source_passage: he gave himself up to the pleasures of imagination. Finally a bright idea flashed across his brain. Why not convert imagination into reality?
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Further meditations induced in him'
findings.why_it_matters: The extended comic interior monologue about ambushing Conrad — with its mock-heroic self-intoxication, 'one would, of course, be careful not to hit too hard,' and Christie's ironic register — is a voice-establishing passage that defines Tommy's character. The draft jumps straight to the picture coming down from the wall without preserving any of this comic deliberation.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least a sentence or two of Tommy's self-delighting scheming: the economical pleasure, the plan seeming 'simple but excellent,' the fantasy of fist-fighting vs. verbal sparring. This is voice content, not mere plot padding.

findings.source_passage: Not belonging to the type of hero who is famous for awaking in full possession of his faculties, Tommy merely blinked at the ceiling and wondered vaguely where he was.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'The sound of the key turning in the lock awoke him'
findings.why_it_matters: This is a textually distinctive, ironic narratorial aside that gently parodies the thriller-hero convention and defines Christie's comic tone for the whole novel. Its absence flattens the register at a key moment.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the parenthetical: 'Not belonging to the type of hero famous for awaking in full possession of his faculties' — it is short, tonally essential, and compresses to nothing.

findings.source_passage: Such an affair was infinitely more in his line than the verbal encounter of this afternoon. Intoxicated by his plan, Tommy gently unhooked the picture of the Devil and Faust
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Further meditations induced in him'
findings.why_it_matters: The contrast between physical action ('infinitely more in his line') and verbal sparring is both character-defining and thematically resonant throughout the novel. 'Intoxicated by his plan' is Christie's ironic register in miniature. Both are erased.
findings.suggested_fix: Fold in the contrast beat and 'intoxicated by his plan' when the picture comes down from the wall, preserving the self-mocking tone.

findings.source_passage: He felt an economical pleasure that his first plan would not be wasted.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'But there was a more vital question'
findings.why_it_matters: A characteristic Christie ironic aside — 'economical pleasure' is wry and distinctive — that the draft drops entirely, losing a small but telling register beat.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert 'He felt an economical pleasure that his first plan would not be wasted' when Tommy retrieves the picture in the dark; it takes four words and preserves the voice.

findings.source_passage: Tommy felt slightly offended. Then, passing his hand over his face, he laughed. He had not shaved or washed for three days! What a guy he must look.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'He glanced at his watch'
findings.why_it_matters: The comic self-discovery — 'felt slightly offended' by the suspicious policeman, then the laugh — is a small but characteristic Christie moment of deflating self-awareness. The draft reduces this to a passing phrase ('laughed at the thought of his three days' beard') losing the beat of offended dignity.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the mini-sequence: 'felt slightly offended — then laughed — three days without shaving' in its original two-step rhythm.

summary: The draft is substantially faithful and preserves all key dialogue and plot beats; three medium-severity voice-flattening findings (comic interior monologue, hero-parody aside, 'infinitely more in his line' contrast) represent real register losses but no single high-severity signature erasure, so the draft narrowly passes.
